title: About Milpa
text: Who makes Milpa Gardens and why, what its evidence promise means, what’s free, and the languages it speaks.

title: Contested: Spraying plants with dissolved aspirin boosts their immune system and health
text: Aspirin spray isn't a proven plant tonic.

title: Contested: If you buy good compost or bagged soil, your native ground underneath doesn't matter
text: Buying good soil doesn't let you ignore the ground underneath.

title: Refuted: Sprinkling baking soda around tomato plants makes the fruit sweeter
text: Baking soda won't sweeten your tomatoes.

title: Contested: Burying banana peels feeds plants potassium (roses in particular)
text: Banana peels do give up their potassium quickly, but a few peels are an unknown and probably small dose, and nothing shows roses need it.

title: Contested: Basil improves the flavor of adjacent tomatoes
text: The one trial we know of found no difference in flavor, and nobody has proposed how it would work.

title: Contested: Bone meal helps transplants and bulbs put down roots
text: Bone meal isn't a rooting tonic. About bone meal, bulb fertilizer, root booster.

title: Contested: Chives or garlic planted under a fruit tree prevent apple scab
text: There's no evidence that chives or garlic under an apple tree prevent scab, and no mechanism for it.

title: Contested: Cinnamon or chamomile tea prevents damping-off in seedlings
text: Cinnamon and chamomile tea are popular anti-damping-off remedies because cinnamon is antifungal in a lab dish.

title: Contested: Coffee grounds acidify soil
text: Coffee grounds haven't been shown to reliably lower soil pH, so they won't durably acidify your soil or make it blueberry-friendly.

title: Contested: Coffee grounds scattered around plants repel slugs, snails, and other pests
text: Coffee grounds scattered around plants haven't been shown to repel slugs or other pests.

title: Refuted: Companion planting charts encode real relationships
text: Most companion-planting advice you'll find online is folklore, and the charts have no scientific basis.

title: Contested: Compost tea (or manure tea) greatly boosts growth and suppresses plant disease
text: Compost tea isn't the tonic or disease cure it's sold as.

title: Refuted: Spreading cornmeal on soil or lawns cures fungal disease
text: Don't use cornmeal as a fungicide. About cornmeal fungicide, cornmeal lawn, cornmeal brown patch.

title: Refuted: Dish soap makes a safe, effective homemade insecticide, the same as insecticidal soap
text: Dish soap isn't the same as insecticidal soap.

title: Refuted: Crushed eggshells in the planting hole prevent blossom-end rot
text: Eggshells in the planting hole won't stop blossom-end rot.

title: Contested: Crushed eggshells deter slugs
text: Crushed eggshells haven't been shown to deter slugs. About eggshells, slugs, slug barrier.

title: Refuted: Epsom salts prevent blossom-end rot
text: Epsom salts won't stop blossom-end rot. About epsom salts, blossom end rot, blossom-end rot.

title: Refuted: Fresh manure is a safe, ready-to-use fertilizer you can spread straight onto the garden
text: Fresh manure isn't a ready-to-use fertilizer. About fresh manure, raw manure, manure fertilizer.

title: Contested: A layer of gravel or pot shards at the bottom of a container improves drainage
text: The old "never put gravel in the bottom of a pot" rule is overstated.

title: Contested: Sprinkling human hair, soap shavings, or urine around the garden reliably keeps deer and rabbits out
text: Hair, soap and other home-remedy scents aren't a reliable way to keep deer or rabbits out.

title: Contested: Watering with hydrogen peroxide oxygenates the roots and cures root rot
text: Hydrogen peroxide won't oxygenate your roots in any lasting way.

title: Folklore, checked
text: 35 common gardening beliefs, like epsom salts and blossom end rot, eggshells and slugs, coffee grounds and soil pH, and planting by the moon.

title: Contested: Marigolds repel most garden pests and protect the whole garden
text: Marigolds don't protect the whole garden.

title: Contested: Spraying diluted milk on the leaves prevents or cures powdery mildew
text: Milk spray for powdery mildew is one of the few home remedies with some trials behind it.

title: Contested: Planting by lunar phase improves germination and yield
text: No mechanism anyone can name, and the few small trials we found disagree with each other.

title: Refuted: More fertilizer means bigger, healthier plants
text: More fertilizer doesn't mean bigger, healthier plants.

title: Refuted: Radishes deter flea beetles
text: Radishes don't repel flea beetles. About radish, flea beetle, trap crop.

title: Contested: You must rotate every crop to new ground every single year
text: You don't have to move every crop every single year by rule.

title: Refuted: Burying rusty nails adds iron that greens up plants and turns hydrangeas blue
text: Rusty nails won't green up your plants or turn hydrangeas blue.

title: Refuted: Mixing sand into clay soil improves its drainage
text: Don't add sand to clay to "loosen" it.

title: Refuted: Seeds saved from hybrid vegetables grow true to the parent plant
text: Seeds from a hybrid won't grow true to the parent.

title: Refuted: Adding sugar or molasses to the soil makes tomatoes and other fruit sweeter
text: Sugar in the soil won't sweeten your tomatoes.

title: Contested: Talking to your plants, or playing them music, makes them grow better
text: Talking to your plants won't grow them faster.

title: Contested: Household vinegar is an effective weed killer
text: Vinegar only burns the parts of a weed it touches, so it works on tiny seedlings, but bigger and perennial weeds grow back from the roots.

title: Contested: Watering a little every day is the best way to water a garden
text: Watering a little every day usually isn't best.

title: Refuted: Watering plants in the midday sun scorches the leaves
text: Watering in the midday sun won't scorch your leaves.
